name: General Oral Health — Conditions, Prevention & Early Care
description: Clinically oriented overview of common, early-stage oral health conditions and prevention approaches—covering halitosis, dental plaque, tooth sensitivity, enamel wear, gingivitis, and early caries risk. Includes risk factors, signs/symptoms, guideline-aligned care options, and references to international professional bodies.
keywords: oral hygiene, plaque, halitosis, gingivitis, dentin hypersensitivity, enamel wear, erosion, scaling and polishing, fluoride, chlorhexidine, prevention

hasPart.name: Halitosis
hasPart.description: Persistent unpleasant oral odor commonly associated with tongue coating, plaque accumulation, xerostomia, or periodontal inflammation.
signOrSymptom: Unpleasant breath noted on waking or after meals

possibleTreatment.name: Short-term antiseptic rinse (e.g., chlorhexidine as indicated)

guideline.name: Professional assessment with hygiene optimization and tongue cleaning

hasPart.name: Dental Plaque (Biofilm)
hasPart.description: Soft biofilm on tooth surfaces that drives gingival inflammation and caries when not regularly disrupted.
hasPart.cause: Biofilm-mediated process with fermentable carbohydrate exposure and inadequate mechanical disruption.

possibleTreatment.name: Toothbrushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste

guideline.name: Daily mechanical plaque control plus professional prophylaxis as indicated

hasPart.name: Dentin Hypersensitivity
hasPart.description: Short, sharp pain from exposed dentin in response to thermal, tactile, osmotic or chemical stimuli in otherwise healthy teeth.
hasPart.differentialDiagnosis: Reversible pulpitis, cracked tooth, caries, defective restoration margins.
signOrSymptom: Pain on air stimulus during examination

possibleTreatment.name: Desensitizing toothpaste (e.g., potassium nitrate; stannous fluoride)
Fluoride varnish or resin sealant on exposed dentin
Technique & diet modification to reduce erosive/abrasive triggers

guideline.name: Rule out pathology; start with non-invasive desensitizing agents

hasPart.name: Enamel Wear / Erosion
hasPart.description: Loss of enamel from chemical erosion (acidic exposure) or mechanical wear; often multifactorial.
hasPart.cause: Intrinsic/extrinsic acids, parafunction (bruxism), abrasive brushing, or dietary habits.
signOrSymptom: Smooth, glossy enamel loss on palatal/lingual surfaces

possibleTreatment.name: Dietary counseling; night guard for bruxism

guideline.name: Identify erosive source and adopt preventive/occlusal protection before restorations

hasPart.name: Gingivitis (Plaque-Induced)
hasPart.description: Reversible inflammation of gingival tissues without attachment loss, typically driven by plaque biofilm.

possibleTreatment.name: Scaling and polishing; professional oral hygiene instruction
Twice-daily brushing with fluoride toothpaste; interdental cleaning

hasPart.epidemiology: Highly prevalent and reversible with adequate plaque control.

guideline.name: Biofilm disruption and risk control; reassess bleeding indices

hasPart.name: Early Caries Risk (Non-cavitated)
hasPart.description: Demineralization of enamel without cavitation due to sustained biofilm-sugar-acid cycles; amenable to non-invasive remineralization.
signOrSymptom: Chalky white spot near gingival margin

possibleTreatment.name: Topical fluoride varnish or high-fluoride toothpaste as indicated
Dietary counseling to reduce cariogenic frequency
Sealants or resin infiltration where appropriate

guideline.name: Non-invasive remineralization strategies prioritized; restorations only if cavitated
